sections.h2: Who records deeds in Tipton County
sections.html:
The county Register of Deeds records deeds and other instruments the law requires or allows to be filed (Tennessee Code 66-24-101). The office is in Covington. Mail goes to PO Box 626, Covington, TN 38019, and deed questions are answered at 901-476-0204.

The list of recordable papers includes deeds, powers of attorney, mortgages, marriage settlements, plats and military discharges. The Register also collects and accounts for the fees and taxes that go with each filing. For a home sale, that normally means the deed from seller to buyer and, when the buyer borrows, the lender's mortgage or deed of trust. Both documents go through the same counter and are charged the fees below. Ask the title company or closing attorney who will deliver them.

Call before a closing to ask about current hours and whether the office accepts electronic filing. Property record lookup is separate: the Assessor's parcel search is at tiptontn.geopowered.com/PropertySearch.

The county uses the standard Tennessee schedule. An ordinary instrument of one or two pages is $10.00, and each page after the second is $5.00. Add a $2.00 data processing fee per document and a $1.00 clerk's fee whenever state tax is paid.

Tipton County recording fees
Document or serviceFee
Instrument of one or two pages$10.00
Each additional page after two$5.00
Plat$15.00
Data processing, per document$2.00
Clerk's fee, only when state tax is paid$1.00
Certified copy, per page$1.00
Military dischargeNo charge

A release or assignment added to an instrument costs $5.00 for each one after the first, which matters when a payoff and a new loan are recorded together. UCC fixture filings are $13.00, and UCC filings over 10 pages add $0.50 per page.

The Register's counter also collects two state taxes. One is the realty transfer tax, set at 37 cents for each $100 of the price. The other is the mortgage tax at 11.5 cents for each $100 of debt, and the first $2,000 of debt is exempt. The county's fee list labels these the conveyance tax and the mortgage tax. Both are separate from the recording fees in the table above. Together with the recording fee, the data processing fee and the clerk's fee, these are all the charges a typical sale deed meets at the Register's counter.

Who pays which tax is set in the purchase contract and shown on the settlement statement, so confirm it with the closing agent before signing. If you want a net sheet that is right to the dollar, ask the title company to show the transfer tax line in advance. County property tax is a separate matter handled by the Trustee, and the Register does not collect it.

sections.h2: Does recording change who gets the tax notice?
sections.html:
It can. Each October the Trustee mails the notice to whoever held title on January 1. A deed recorded in time for the September cutoff also triggers a second copy to the buyer. A buyer whose deed lands later may see no bill at all and should call the Trustee at 901-476-0211.

That office also posts the numbers a buyer will care about: a 2026 county rate of $1.3417, residential assessment at 25 percent, interest-free payment through February 28, and monthly interest after that. Before a deed goes to the Register, work through this short checklist:

  • Get the Trustee's status on the parcel for the current year
  • Find out whether a city bill, such as Covington's, is also open
  • Check that the legal description and parcel number match the deed
  • Ask the Register's office how it takes payment of the recording fee and state tax

The county's "Where Do I" page sorts common requests by office, which helps when a sale turns up a question that is not a recording matter. The Register handles copies of deeds and plats and the recording of a deed or other document. Other pieces of a sale sit elsewhere:

  • Tax maps, property assessment values and the Greenbelt Program: Property Assessor
  • Paying property taxes: Trustee
  • Tax sale auctions: Chancery Court
  • Rezoning and zoning of county properties: Planning and Development
  • Obtaining a new address: TCECD 911

The Assessor also keeps the parcel history, tracking property sales, building permits and zoning changes when updating the roll, so a recorded deed feeds into the Assessor's records. A buyer who needs a corrected mailing address for the tax bill should contact the Assessor at 901-476-0213.

The Register offers a free Property Fraud Alert through its computer vendor. Once an owner enrolls, an email arrives whenever a document is recorded under a name the owner has added. A seller who just closed, or an heir managing a family house, can use it to watch for filings under the old owner's name. The enrollment steps are:

  • Have a valid email address ready
  • Go to www.mylandalert.com and click Register in the upper left
  • Accept the terms at the bottom of the page and enter the email address
  • Click the verification link, choose a password, and add the names to watch

sections.h2: Preparing for a Tipton County closing
sections.html:
A sale involves a few offices in a set order. First confirm the tax status with the Trustee, then have the title company or attorney prepare the deed. The signed deed, with the fees and state tax, goes to the Register, and the recorded deed then feeds the Assessor's records. If the buyer borrows, the lender's mortgage or deed of trust is recorded alongside it and a payoff release for your old loan follows.

Close to a sale, ask three things. Who is delivering the documents to Covington? Which party covers the transfer tax under the contract? Does the parcel carry a city bill as well as a county bill? A cash sale leaves out the lender's paperwork and the mortgage tax, so the recording packet is shorter and the fees are mostly the deed charges above. Keep the recorded deed with your closing papers for later reference.

Bring or send the originals only. Copies are not a substitute for the signed deed, and a deed missing a page can hold up the whole filing. If a certified copy of an older deed is needed for the sale, the Register charges $1.00 per page, so ask for it a few days before closing rather than the day of. Plats cost $15.00 to record, which applies mostly to new subdivisions and not to a resale of an existing house.

faqs.q: Which office accepts a deed for recording in Tipton County?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds in Covington. The office mails to PO Box 626, Covington, TN 38019, and answers deed questions at 901-476-0204.

faqs.q: What fees apply when a Tipton County deed is recorded?
faqs.a: The base charge is $10.00 for up to two pages, with $5.00 for every page beyond that, a $2.00 data processing fee, and a $1.00 clerk's fee whenever state tax is paid.

faqs.q: How big is the state tax on a Tipton County sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $0.37 for each $100 of the price. Your title company can work out the exact figure for your sale.

faqs.q: Does a Tipton County loan carry its own tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The state mortgage tax is $0.115 for each $100 of debt beyond the first $2,000.

faqs.q: Is there a free warning when something is filed under my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register sponsors a free fraud alert at mylandalert.com. Once you enroll a name, an email arrives each time a document is filed under it.
